# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 79 (Bu-Vb Pc79)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc79
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 79
**Title (English, from literature):** Criticizing a legitimate legal procedure
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 79 (*Kammapaṭibāhana*) establishes an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for any monastic who gives consent (*chanda*) to a legitimate legal procedure (*dhammakamma*) of the Saṅgha and subsequently criticizes or challenges it [Hüsken 1997]. In the narrative background, monks raise objections (*patikkosati*) while a formal act is underway [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga_]. The rule addresses the tendency to change one's mind capriciously and undermine properly executed communal acts; it applies equally to monks and nuns, corresponding to Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 157 [Hüsken 1997]. Scholarly analysis connects Pācittiya 79 to related rules that prohibit disputing or reopening legitimate settlements, such as Pācittiya 63 or Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 76, which specifically concerns formal acts carried out by a motion and one announcement (*ñattidutiyakamma*) [Hüsken 1997].

 A modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates that this rule shares extensive formulaic legal material across 87 Pali texts, most prominently with the *Campeyyakkhandhaka* (Kd 9) concerning formal acts and other Pācittiya rules dealing with legal procedures (notably Pc 21, Pc 63, Pc 28, and Pc 76) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic textual alignments with the Tibetan *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā-vinayasamuccaya* (D4106) [DharmaNexus].
